chapter_theme: The body of Thiruvalluvar Njanam, nineteen short verses attributed to Thiruvalluvar but not his: a Siddhar speaks in the first person of his making in the womb, his destruction of the slur of low birth, and the secret no one sees, then preaches impermanence (the cremation ground ends every life), the root whirl and release, the fruit of kaya siddhi, and a run of cipher verses on salt, urine and the moon that read as rejuvenation (karpam) formulas. The Valluvar name is a late attribution; the matter is Siddha medicine and yoga.
structure_note: 1623 to 1625 are autobiographical and claim a secret the world does not see; 1626 to 1631 preach impermanence, each ending in the burning ground or the perishing body; 1632 to 1636 give the way, nectar, the whirl, the Veda's inner sense, karma burned, kaya siddhi; 1637 to 1639 are salt verses in cipher; 1640 and 1641 close on mastering the five elements and gaining siddhi without leaving the body. The metres shift from kattalaikkalitturai through kochchagam to venba, which the tool records under one காப்பு heading.

1623.reading: Having come into the womb called mother and stayed there, I remained well inside for ten months; what wonder: I was formed with all the heights that are set in this world, and they do not see the truth.
1623.nuance: The claim is the Siddhar doctrine that the body formed in the womb holds everything the world holds (உன்னதமெல்லாம் அமைந்தேன்), so the truth is to be found in it. The verse begins a first-person life story that ends in 1625 with the secret no one sees.

1624.reading: Born on the earth, having studied and known the language, caught by the charm of the world's people and parted from it, whirling in the pit, I trusted for some days the golden lotus of the kundalini; they do not see the secret.
1624.nuance: கும்பி is both the hell Kumbhipaka and the belly, so the pit may be the world's suffering or the body; the golden lotus of the kundalini is the root centre. ரகசியம், the secret, is left unsaid and is the refrain of these three verses (காண்கிலரே, they do not see).

1625.reading: The cosmos, the sky and the earth, and the inner meaning of the Agamas, I know clearly and shining within this body; I destroyed the way in which the gadflies called me low-born; they do not see the clear sense of the secret that I opened.
1625.nuance: நீசன் என்ற வாறு, the way they called me low-born, draws on the legend of Valluvar's outcaste birth, and the verse answers it not by argument but by knowledge of the cosmos in the body. வண்டர் (gadflies, or louts) is the only word spent on the accusers.

1626.reading: Men born into the world: your life, which you took to be real, how does its stirring show itself? Living without doubt in the world, wearing the esteem of manliness, this life called a lie goes to the burning ground.
1626.nuance: The question in line 2 is the real content: what makes the body move is not seen, and so what is taken as real (மெய்) is called a lie (பொய்). சுடுகாடு, the burning ground, ends this and the next four verses.

1627.reading: In the house of release, in the house of the sound at the root whirl, the bindu shines, and by it the long sea-girt world flourishes and grows and stands bright; what use to seek a treasure-house that is the thing destroyed by not seeking; they do not see that the land one reaches is the forest of the burning ground.
1627.nuance: மூலச் சுழி, the root whirl, and நாத வீடு, the house of sound, locate release in the body's base where bindu (seed, or the drop of light) shines. The third line is hard: பொக்கிடம் is a treasure-house and தேடாதழித்த பொருள் a thing lost by not seeking; the sense may be that the bindu spent in the world is lost, and only the burning ground remains.

1628.reading: Though one reaches the seven kinds of birth and the four kinds of womb, by the teaching that it is the thing of pouring blood, sound and seed, as it passes and passes the sea of lives wanes like the waning moon, and having seen it, the great earth, however long it stays, is impermanent.
1628.nuance: எழுவகைத் தோற்றம், நால்வகை யோனி are the traditional seven orders of birth and four wombs (egg, womb, sweat, seed). சுரோணிதம் நாதவிந்து is the womb-blood and seed from which bodies come; the verse's claim is that all births are only that substance passing, and so impermanent. The grammar of the middle lines is loose.

1629.reading: However long one lives, this body perishes by itself as it was ordered before, not knowing it; the father's decree makes it so; thinking on how body, life and frame perish and cease, having seen that former order, do they still not know?
1629.nuance: அனுப்படி (as ordered) is repeated and தந்தைவிதி, the father's decree, names the ordering as the Lord's; the verse is a fate verse in a Siddhar text, where fate is usually something to be overcome (see 1635). The line-breaks are garbled and the subject of the last line is unclear.

1630.reading: Desire for the womb does not die; your life is impermanent; is there in that honey-pot a bliss beyond pleasure? In small pleasure, when the flesh is gone and the body is gone and goes, knowing nothing, for the low there is no heaven but the burning ground.
1630.nuance: சுகாதீதம், beyond pleasure, is the word for the bliss of release; the verse asks whether sex gives it and answers with the burning ground. The target is lust alone; the body's other appetites are not mentioned.

1631.reading: This body dies in this world, a life that does not know the way it came; this body, will it come to rule the wish-tree that is the serpent lying in a small pit? See.
1631.nuance: அரவம் அற்பக் குழியில், the serpent in a small pit, is the coiled power at the root centre, and கற்பகம், the wish-granting tree, what it gives when ruled. On this reading the verse asks whether a body that does not know its own origin can master the kundalini. A plain reading (the body's hopes are as vain as a snake in a hole ruling a wish-tree) also stands.

1632.reading: ... drinking that drink out of hunger; if one sees knowledge, body, life and frame grow strong; if one eats, eat the nectar juice.
1632.nuance: The first line of the venba is missing, so what drink (பானம்) is meant is lost. அமிர்தரசம், the nectar juice, in the Siddhars is the fluid held to come from the head in yoga, or a prepared karpam; the verse ties bodily strength to seeing knowledge, which is the Siddhar claim that jnana feeds the body.

1633.reading: What is there for those who do not know the whirl, what for those who do not know the bliss, what for those who do not know the way to reach it; for those who, not knowing the whirl, do not know the root and do not attain release on that path, Yama is Death: for them there is dying. See.
1633.nuance: சுழி (the whirl) and மூலம் (the root) are the technical words, the opening of the central channel and the base centre. The verse states the Siddhar position flatly: death is for those who do not know the whirl, so release is deathlessness in the body.

1634.reading: If the hidden knowledge of the Veda becomes true perception itself, by the Lord's grace one seeks the state; among the four meanings of the Veda's secret, see the good meaning as the ghee churned from milk.
1634.nuance: An unusually friendly verse to the Veda for a Siddhar text, but conditional: only when its hidden sense (மறைஞானம்) becomes மெய்யுணர்வு. நாலு பொருள் may be the four ends (virtue, wealth, pleasure, release) or the four Vedas; the ghee-from-milk image makes the good sense an essence extracted from the whole.

1635.reading: I burned the fate-deed that was there from the first and the triple void, and toiled with an unpanicked mind; born without regard to the good deeds and bad deeds there from the first, I sent my life off out of the strong deeds.
1635.nuance: ஊழ்வினையை ... சுட்டு, burning fate-deed, is a claim to have destroyed karma, and முப்பாழ் (the three voids) is burned with it. The last line is ambiguous: வல்வினையிற் போக்கிவிட்டேன் வாழ்வு may mean 'I freed my life from strong deeds' or 'I wasted my life in strong deeds'; the first fits the boast of the verse.

1636.reading: After the siddhi of the body drove off my karma-deeds, the siddhi of maya and the root whirl will come to me; by the siddhi of the body, by the root tamarind, the first initiation was done; now see it in two years' time.
1636.nuance: காயசித்தி is the deathless or perfected body, and மாயசித்தி here probably the powers over appearance. மூலப் புளி (root tamarind, or root acid) is unexplained; tradition reads புளி in Siddha cipher as a prepared acid or as a body-substance, so the first diksha may be a medicine rather than a rite. The two-year term is the kind of stated period the karpam verses give.

1637.reading: Not knowing the thought behind the rock salt that comes, humans eat and fall into strong deeds and die; though rock salt, white rock salt, comes in many kinds, think that it is in the inner mind.
1637.nuance: கல்லுப்பு (rock salt) is a common Siddhar cipher; tradition takes salt variously as a body-fluid, as the alchemical salt, or as the taste of the world one eats and dies of. The last line, that the salt is 'in the mind' (உள்ளமதில் உண்டு), argues against a literal mineral and for a cipher. The verse makes a claim about where the substance is, not a preparation.

1638.reading: It is always rock salt in this body of eight spans; what is the reason that, seeing it, they do not know it? Always the moon: drawing off that urine, setting it on fire and heating it, I realise the truth as strength.
1638.nuance: அமுரி is the Siddha medical word for urine, used in rejuvenation (amuri karpam), and இந்துப்பு (rock salt) is tied to இந்து, the moon, by sound. The verse claims the body already holds the substance (எண்சாண் உடல், the eight-span body) and that heating it gives strength; a coded reading takes the moon's fluid as the nectar from the head. This is a claim about a substance, recorded as history, not as a remedy.

1639.reading: Because the dross of the salt changed as it oozed, before old age turns it to calx; by the salt this body hardens for crores of aeons, and in the vaasi that leaps at a word, the body.
1639.nuance: சுன்னம் (calx, the calcined ash) is an alchemical end-product and here what old age makes of the body; the salt properly treated is claimed to keep the body for கற்பாந்தம் கோடி, crores of kalpas. The last line brings in வாசி, the breath practice, so the hardened body is kept by breath as well as by salt; the syntax is broken and the reading is a reconstruction.

1640.reading: If one knows the five elements, the five that seem impermanent come under control within the year; those who see and know the five, in the memory of the vision of knowledge, may come to know the opened decree.
1640.nuance: அஞ்சு வசப்படுவது, the five coming under control, is the mastery of the elements (பூதஜயம்) counted among the siddhis. ஆண்டதனில் (in the year) may be a time limit or a slip; விதி, decree, is here something opened and known rather than suffered.

1641.reading: Taking a body of eight spans, what of it, my Lord? Removing the nearness of women, there is great bliss; so that the eye may see, without the body ceasing, the knowledge that gains siddhi, the siddhi of yoga ... decree: think on it.
1641.nuance: தேகம் ஒழியாமல் சித்தி பெறும் ஞானம், the knowledge that gains siddhi without the body ceasing, is the text's statement of its goal: release in the living body. போசைவிதி is an obscure word, perhaps a corruption; the sense of the last foot is lost.

links.note: Sivavakkiyar asks what a Paraiyar woman is and what a Brahmin woman is, finding no mark on flesh or bone; the Valluvar text answers the slur of low birth from the other side, by knowing the cosmos in the body and so destroying the way they called him low.

The Naladiyar says good and bad caste are only words and that austerity and learning make a lineage; the Siddhar text makes knowledge of the cosmos in the body the thing that destroys the charge of low birth. Both answer caste with attainment, in the ethical and the yogic domains.

The Kural asks what is stronger than fate, which gets ahead of any other plan; the text that borrows Valluvar's name says it burned the fate-deed that was there from the first. On the reading that 1635 claims karma itself destroyed, the two are incompatible; the Kural's own 620 (seeing fate's back by toil) is the nearer relative.
Kural 620 says the untiring will see fate's back; 1635 turns that into the Siddhar claim of burning fate-deed and the triple void outright by unpanicked effort.

Both say the one who does not open the inner door perishes: Tirumular says one becomes weak if the inner door is not opened; this text says Yama is Death for those who do not know the whirl and the root.

Kaka Pusundar's chapter turns from silence to buying rock salt and opens an alchemical sequence; here rock salt is the thing humans eat and die of and is said to be in the mind. Both use கல்லுப்பு as a cipher whose referent the text never gives.

Tirumular's Siva-water drunk for a year makes the body shine and turn gold; here the moon's urine drawn off and heated gives strength. Both are claims about a fluid of the body as the medicine of the body, and tradition reads both as cipher for the yogic nectar.
Both make leaving women the precondition of the bliss of release: Romarishi will speak the path only to one who has left desire for women, and here great bliss comes once their nearness is removed.

source_issues: 1632 has three lines; the first line of the venba is missing.
1629 and 1639 have broken syntax and word division (தந்தைவிதி உன்னலழிவ துடலுயிர்; சொற்பாயும் வாசியில் தேகம்); the readings are reconstructions.
1641 போசைவிதி is an unknown form, probably corrupt.
The tool labels every unit of this work காப்பு though only 1622 is an invocation; the metres named (கட்டளைக் கலித்துறை, தரவு கொச்சகம், நேரிசை வெண்பா) are given in the second half of the label.
